summary: Masakazu Tanaka works in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Tohoku University (~1974–1980) and earned his Ph.D. at the London School of Economics and University of London (~1980–1986). His career includes positions at Kyoto University (1988–2019) and the Professional Institute of International Fashion (2019).

Masako Keta is a philosopher and religious studies scholar. She studied at Kyoto University (~1971–1975, ~1977–1982) under Yoshinori Takeuchi. Her career includes posts at Hamamatsu University School of Medicine (1975–1977), Kanazawa University (1988, 1998), and Kyoto University (2000–2018).
Masamichi Asukai was a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1953 to 1957 and later held a post there from ~1975 to 1998.

Masamichi Ichigo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University, Kyoto University, and the University of Michigan, working under Susumu Yamaguchi, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Gadjin M. Nagao. He held posts at Kyoto Sangyo University, Otani University, and Kyoto Koka Women's University.

Masamichi Sakai specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under Helmut Krasser (2006, attested 2010) and held an associate professorship at Kansai University (attested 2015).
Masanori Nakagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1991) and associate professor of literature (attested 2002) at Chikushi Jogakuen University.
Masanori Shono specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. His career includes posts at Osaka University (attested 2012) and the University of Munich (attested 2015).

Masao Abe was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Osaka City University, Kyoto University, Union Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under scholars including Hajime Tanabe and Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. He taught at Nara University and Kyoto University.
Masao Shizutani was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He held associate professor posts at Josai University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1974).

Masao Yamaguchi was a scholar of religious studies and other fields. He studied at Tokyo Metropolitan University and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1965–1989), University of Shizuoka (1994), and Sapporo University (1997–1999).
Masaru Akimoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at Kyoto Women's University, including as professor of the Faculty of Contemporary Society (attested 2002, 2015).

Masashi Nagai is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University (~1965–1969, doctorate 1998) and later served there as a lecturer (1984), associate professor (1988, 1994), professor emeritus (2017), and president (2019).
Masataka Suzuki is a scholar of religious studies and other fields. He studied at Keio University from ~1968 to 1978 and later held a post there from ~1984 to 2015.

Masataro Sawayanagi was a scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1885–1888). He later held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1901–1910), Tohoku University (~1911–1913), Kyushu University (~1913–1914), and Taisho University (~1926–1927).

Masato Kobayashi specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1989–1995) and completed his Ph.D. under George Cardona at the University of Pennsylvania (~1995–2000). He was a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2000–2005).

Masatoshi Konishi was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at International Christian University, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Hosei University (1971–1984) and Rikkyo University (1984–2003).

Masatoshi Nagatomi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, Kyoto University, and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. Nagatomi spent his academic career at Harvard University, becoming an instructor in 1958 and professor in 1969.

Masayuki Taira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1980) and held posts at Osaka University (~1994–2012), Kansai University, and Kyoto Tachibana University (~2012).

Massimo Pallottino was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1927–1931) and held academic posts at the University of Cagliari (~1945–1947) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1947–1980).
Masumi Mochizuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held posts at Minobusan University, serving as a lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhism (attested 2001) and later as a professor (attested 2015).
